theorem.base_root_transfer: For x in the base support X, the transfer has a_x L_Q(x)=Omega_x Q(x).  Since a_x and Omega_x are nonzero, a forced split-locator root L_Q(x)=0 is equivalent to Q(x)=0.
theorem.finite_slope_bound: For each compatible Q-class, the direction equations are inconsistent, slope-free/contained, or determine one scalar z.  Thus the nonzero-quadratic branch has at most two finite noncontained parameters.
theorem.low_degree_transfer: At A=385 every finite root in a separated rank-6 boundary bucket is represented by a projective Q-class with deg Q<5.
theorem.projective_safety: The endpoint-uniform theorem contributes at most the single projective endpoint, so the branch total is at most 3<=6.
theorem.quadratic_cut: For direction nodes y,y', the equality of the two displayed ratios is N_y(Q)D_y'(Q)-N_y'(Q)D_y(Q)=0.  On the residual Q-line this is a binary quadratic.  If one such quadratic is not identically zero, every compatible finite root lies among at most two projective Q-classes.
theorem.residual: If every pairwise direction-consistency quadratic vanishes identically on the fixed three-core Q-line, the branch remains as the ratio-identically-consistent fixed-three-core residual.
theorem.three_point_reduction: Evaluation at three distinct base nodes has rank three on polynomials deg Q<5.  After factoring the fixed three-point core E, Q=E R with deg R<2, so the residual Q-space is a projective line.
